details: For every nonempty finite binary class, with Yang dimension computed over $\mathbb F_2$, $\mathrm{sd}(\mathcal H)\leq2\,\mathrm{Y}_{\mathbb F_2}(\mathcal H)-1$; equivalently $\mathrm{Y}_{\mathbb F_2}(\mathcal H)\geq(\mathrm{sd}(\mathcal H)+1)/2$.
proof: The antipodal realizable-distribution complex is the intersection of the Yang complex with its label flip. Its coindex is at most its Stiefel--Whitney height, then at most its Stanley--Reisner regularity minus one; the Kalai--Meshulam regularity inequality bounds that regularity by twice the Yang dimension.
proof_source: Full proof in the local Yang-dimension draft: ~/latex/YangDim/drafts/spherical_dimension.tex, Theorem `thm:sd-vs-hd` (unpublished).
witness_verification: For the singleton family, Yang dimension is n-1 while spherical dimension is 1 for n>=3. Thus no reverse affine-linear bound of Yang dimension by spherical dimension can hold.
name: Yang Dimension / Spherical Dimension (affine)
